fields.questionText: A teacher computed the mean marks of 40 students from a grouped frequency distribution and obtained Σfi = 40 and Σfixi = 1680. Later she found that the frequencies of two classes had been interchanged: the class with class mark 45 had been recorded as 8 instead of 5, and the class with class mark 25 had been recorded as 5 instead of 8. Find the incorrect mean and the correct mean.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Correction: class mark 45 has 3 too many (remove 3 × 45 = 135); class mark 25 has 3 too few (add 3 × 25 = 75). Correct Σfixi = 1680 − 135 + 75 = 1620; Σfi stays 40.

rationale: Authored row was indeterminate (no class mark; Σf would no longer be 40; answer a range). Re-authored with given class marks and an interchange keeping Σf = 40; solved: 42 → 40.5.

solutionSteps: Choose modal class 20-30 (so l = 20, h = 10) and target mode = 25.
Mode = l + ((f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)) × h = 20 + ((f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)) × 10 = 25.
So (f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) = 1/2 ⇒ 2(f₁ − f₀) = 2f₁ − f₀ − f₂ ⇒ f₂ = f₀.
Pick f₀ = 5 (class 10-20), f₁ = 11 (class 20-30, the largest) and f₂ = 5 (class 30-40); give class 0-10 frequency 0. Distribution: 0-10 → 0, 10-20 → 5, 20-30 → 11, 30-40 → 5.
Check: highest frequency 11 is in 20-30, so it is the modal class. Mode = 20 + ((11 − 5)/(22 − 5 − 5)) × 10 = 20 + (6/12) × 10 = 25. ✓

rationale: Steps 4–5 carried a leaked trial (f₁ = 12, f₂ = 4 → 24.67) contradicting the final 0, 5, 11, 5. Rewrote them to the final distribution; verified Mode = 20 + (6/12)×10 = 25.

fields.questionText:
A teacher records the weekly test scores (out of 25) of five students in her class: 18, 20, 15, 22, 15. Based on this information, answer the following questions:
(i) What is the mode of the scores? (1 mark)
(ii) Find the median score. (1 mark)
(iii) Find the mean score and state whether it is greater than, less than or equal to the median. (2 marks)
fields.answer: (i) Mode = 15 (ii) Median = 18 (iii) Mean = 18; the mean is equal to the median.
fields.explanation: Arrange in ascending order: 15, 15, 18, 20, 22. 15 occurs twice, so the mode is 15. The middle (3rd) value is 18, so the median is 18. Sum = 90, so the mean is 90/5 = 18, which equals the median.
solutionSteps: (i) Arrange in ascending order: 15, 15, 18, 20, 22; 15 occurs most often, so mode = 15. [1]
(ii) n = 5 (odd), so the median is the 3rd value = 18. [1]
(iii) Mean = 18 = median, so the mean is equal to the median. [1]

rationale: Authored Section-E row had no case sub-parts. Restructured into a case with (i)(ii)(iii) = 1+1+2 on the same data; steps sum to 4. Verified mode 15, median 18, mean 18. Difficulty Easy (direct computation).

solutionSteps: [1 mark] (b) n/2 = 25; cumulative frequencies 5, 13, 25, 40, 50; the first cf greater than 25 is 40, so the median class is 30-40 (median = 30 + ((25 − 25)/15) × 10 = 30).
[1 mark] (c) Modal class = 30-40 (highest frequency 15): l = 30, f₁ = 15, f₀ = 12, f₂ = 10, h = 10.
fields.finalAnswer: (a) Mean = 28.4 marks (b) Median class 30-40 (c) Mode = 33.75 marks

rationale: Added the missing marking scheme (1 + 1 + 2 = 4) matching the existing answer. Verified Σfx = 1420 → mean 28.4; median class 30-40; mode = 33.75.
Question is about mode / modal class, not step-deviation mean; subtopic relabelled. Content and A–R verdict unchanged.

fields.questionText: A right circular cone has volume 13,600 cm³ and base radius 20 cm. Find the angle which the slant height makes with the base radius. (Take π = 3 and √3 = 1.7.)
fields.strategyHint: Find h from the volume, then use tan θ = h/r in the right triangle formed by the height, radius and slant height.

rationale: Cone figure's only datum (radius 20 cm) is carried by the row's steps/hint, so stated it in text. The OR part (two right triangles, figure-only, trig) is unrecoverable and dropped. Verified h = 34, tan θ = 1.7 = √3 → 60°.

fields.questionText:
Two rectangular sheets, each of dimensions 45 cm × 155 cm, are folded to make hollow right circular cylindrical pipes, with exactly 1 cm overlap when sticking the ends. Sheet 1 is folded along its length (so its height is 155 cm) and Sheet 2 along its width (so its height is 45 cm). Both pipes are closed at both ends.
(i) Find the difference in the curved surface areas of the two cylinders.
(ii) Find the ratio of the volumes of the two cylinders formed. (Use π = 22/7.)
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Sheet 1: height h₁ = 155 cm, circumference = 45 − 1 = 44 cm. Sheet 2: height h₂ = 45 cm, circumference = 155 − 1 = 154 cm.
[1 mark] (i) CSA = circumference × height: CSA₁ = 44 × 155 = 6820 cm², CSA₂ = 154 × 45 = 6930 cm²; difference = 6930 − 6820 = 110 cm².
fields.strategyHint: The side along which the sheet is folded becomes the height; the other side minus the 1 cm overlap becomes the circumference.

rationale: (ii) had no value ('from MS'); solved: 124 : 441. OR variant depends on a figure ('geometry shown') with no dimensions in text — dropped. Main variant re-stepped to 5 marks; verified CSAs 6820/6930 (Δ110).
π rendered as 'p' and page-code '1430/4/1' leaked into option D; restored. TSA of solid hemisphere = 3πr², so ratio 3π : 1 (option c).

fields.questionText: Two identical solid cubes of side 'a' are joined end to end. The total surface area of the resulting cuboid is:
solutionSteps: The cuboid is 2a × a × a; TSA = 2(2a·a + a·a + 2a·a) = 10a² (or 2 × 6a² − 2a² for the two hidden faces). Correct option: (b) 10a².

rationale: 'endtoend', lost superscripts (a2) and stray mark '1' cleaned. Verified TSA = 12a² − 2a² = 10a².
